title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
gist: Security firm Claroc found SpaceXSI's Grok Build vibe-coding agent exposes thousands of user apps, including 24 of SpaceXSI's own internal apps and data from Fortune 500 firms and a defense contractor, because share-link randomness sits in the subdomain where passive DNS enumerates it; ~95% of 43,601 grok.me links were public. The same flaw affects Lovable, Bolt, and Replit, while Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini share links put randomness in the path.

insights.claim: Grok Build, the vibe-coding agent from SpaceXSI (the merged SpaceX and xAI), leaked proprietary and sensitive data from thousands of users through shareable app links, per security firm Claroc.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Enterprise security risk from AI-built apps is a liability for SpaceXSI's enterprise push.

insights.claim: A passive DNS search returned 43,601 links ending in grok.me, of which more than 35,000 (nearly 95%) were publicly accessible, exposing the apps and all stored data.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Scale indicates systemic default-setting failure, not isolated user error.
insights.locator: Aprozper said a passive DNS search

insights.claim: Claroc found 24 exposed apps built by SpaceXSI itself, including a confidential onboarding plan for its enterprise sales team, a sales territory map of 594 accounts, internal system addresses, and advertising proposals.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The vendor's own data leaked, undermining trust in its enterprise AI offering.
insights.locator: Ironically, some of the sensitive data

insights.claim: Exposed third-party Grok Build data included a Tesla service-center scorecard naming 22 technicians, a US Navy contractor roster of 108 people, 3,784 worker medical exams, a hospital roster of about 3,565 staff, and about 4,000 vehicle-transport orders with prices and margins.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Breach exposure spans Fortune 500, healthcare, and defense, raising regulatory and litigation risk.

insights.claim: AI-built internal tools can bypass enterprise access controls: a tool bought by a sales team would sit behind company sign-in, but the same tool built with AI went live open to anyone with the link.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Shadow-IT risk from vibe coding is a tailwind for enterprise security vendors and governance tooling.
insights.quote: Built with AI, it went live open to anyone with the link.

themes.theme: Root cause: randomness in the subdomain

insights.claim: Grok Build places share-link randomness in the subdomain left of grok.me rather than in the URL path, so new links are captured by passive DNS databases and can be enumerated; path-based secrets like Google Docs' are invisible to DNS.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: A concrete design anti-pattern to audit in any capability-URL sharing system.

insights.claim: Capability-based access control treats possession of an unguessable URL as authorization; three dice words give roughly 38 bits of entropy, but entropy is useless if the URL leaks via DNS.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Reusable lens: link secrecy depends on where the secret travels, not just its entropy.
insights.locator: The scheme is intended to prevent links

insights.claim: Claroc's tests found Grok Build defaults share links to 'Anyone with the link', contradicting a Cursor representative's claim that Grok Build apps are private by default.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Vendor statements conflict with independent testing, a credibility and regulatory risk for SpaceXSI.

insights.claim: App builders Lovable, Bolt, and Replit also give each app its own subdomain, so the same passive DNS enumeration exposes them, though Grok held by far the most sensitive company data.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: The vibe-coding category broadly carries this data-exposure risk.
insights.quote: However, Grok is where we found by far the most sensitive company data.
insights.locator: The Cursor statement regarding other AI coding platforms

insights.claim: Claude published artifacts, ChatGPT shared conversations, and Gemini share links put the secret randomness in the URL path, so DNS never sees it.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Major chat platforms follow correct practice; differentiation on security for enterprise buyers.

insights.claim: Meta's Muse agent recently suspended a link-sharing feature after it was also found leaking sensitive data.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Link-sharing leaks are a recurring failure mode across AI agent products.

insights.claim: SpaceXSI did not respond to Claroc's notification or tags to Elon Musk and Grok manager Matt Palmer on X, and only removed its own 24 exposed apps within hours of an Ars inquiry, without answering whether it would notify affected customers.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Weak disclosure handling increases regulatory and customer-trust risk.

insights.claim: SpaceXSI recently acquired AI coding service Cursor, whose representative answered press questions about Grok Build.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Cursor is now part of SpaceXSI's coding-agent stack.
